nodes.summary: Plain Python function that runs the three lenses in sequence and assembles the result.

Rule 3: valuation lean vs growth lean

nodes.summary: Labels the tone of one article's headline and summary. It never sees prices or other articles.
does: Returns strict JSON with exactly five keys
Label POSITIVE / NEUTRAL / NEGATIVE with confidence 0–1
Quotes an evidence span of at most 12 words

nodes.summary: Writes a short cross-lens brief from verdicts, tone, sources and disagreements that code already produced.

does: Regex extraction of integers, decimals, comma groups and percentages

nodes.failure: One untraceable number rejects the whole text.

agentView.note: QuantEra has three research lenses today, run in sequence by one function. They are deterministic modules that call a model for bounded subtasks, not autonomous agents. The five dashed lenses are the planned extension.

walkthrough.title: GET /api/research/AAPL
walkthrough.note: A guided reading of the code path in app.py and synthesize(). It is not a live execution trace.

steps.title: Validate and check the cache
steps.body: The route upper-cases the ticker, rejects anything outside 1–10 alphanumeric characters with HTTP 400, and returns a cached response if one under phase5v1:AAPL is younger than 2 hours.

steps.title: Fetch and normalize data
steps.body: DataProvider reads yfinance statements and prices, scales and sanity-checks them, and returns FieldValue-based contracts. A missing line item stays is_present=False.

steps.title: Run fundamentals, then technicals
steps.body: Ratios and indicators are plain Python. EV/EBITDA, interest coverage and all three growth metrics come back UNAVAILABLE for every ticker and are recorded as data notes.

steps.title: Ingest and rank news
steps.body: Finnhub returns 14 days of articles. Only allowlisted outlets survive, near-duplicates are removed, and the top 8 by recency, relevance and ticker match go forward.

steps.title: Classify each article, then aggregate in code
steps.body: The model labels each article separately. Its quoted evidence must appear in the article or the label becomes neutral with zero weight. Overall tone is a confidence-weighted sum computed in Python.

steps.title: Detect disagreements
steps.body: Three fixed rules compare the lenses, for example strong fundamentals against negative news tone. Each match becomes a record with the exact basis that triggered it.

steps.title: Draft the brief and check it
steps.body: The model writes a brief from the already-computed payload. Any number not in that payload, any link to an unretrieved source, or any advice word rejects the whole draft.

steps.title: Fall back if rejected
steps.body: A rejected or failed draft is replaced by a template built only from verdicts and tone. narrative_status tells the client which one it received.

steps.title: Build the graph and respond
steps.body: The graph builder turns validated results and peer tickers into nodes and edges, each with a grounding string. The route caches the payload and returns it to the UI.

vision.title: What we're building
vision.summary: An equity research workbench where every figure traces back to a filing or a price series, every sentence a model writes is checked before it is shown, and missing evidence is reported instead of filled in. Three lenses run today. The target is eight lenses coordinated as a typed graph, on point-in-time data, with a public deployment.

principles.title: Numbers come from code
principles.body: Ratios, indicators, valuations and risk measures are deterministic Python with tests. A model never calculates a figure that reaches the user.

principles.title: Models write inside guards
principles.body: Every model output is checked for untraceable numbers, unretrieved sources and advice language. A failed check means a template, not a softer draft.

principles.title: Gaps stay visible
principles.body: A missing field is marked unavailable and carried to the response as a data note. Nothing is defaulted to zero or inferred.

stages.title: Finish the lenses that exist
stages.body: Compute the three growth metrics from the multi-year statements already fetched, add EBITDA and interest expense to the data contract, and run the test suite on every pull request.

stages.title: Move orchestration to LangGraph
stages.body: A typed ResearchState, lenses fanned out in parallel, grounding as an explicit conditional edge, and per-node timing and routing telemetry. The HTTP contract stays the same.

stages.title: Make provenance point-in-time
stages.body: Ingest SEC company facts with filing dates so analysis can be pinned to what was public on a given day, and bind each generated number to the field it describes.

stages.title: Add five lenses
stages.body: Valuation (DCF, WACC, sensitivity), risk (EWMA volatility, VaR, expected shortfall), macro context, institutional ownership from 13F filings, and multi-ticker portfolio analysis.

stages.title: Deploy it publicly
stages.body: A hosted API and research UI, so the walkthrough on this page can be run against a live ticker.

flow.title: How one request runs
flow.note: Illustrative run. The entity, dates and numbers are example values from the design spec, not results.

nodes.label: Request
nodes.built: Today the API takes a ticker. The as_of date and horizon are part of the design.

nodes.sub: SEC XBRL, prices, news, 13F, ALFRED vintages

steps.title: A request arrives
steps.body: A research question enters the graph as structured input: which company, as of which date, over which horizon.
steps.graph: The graph's input is a typed ResearchState, not a free-form prompt.

request: Analyze ENT_000412 as of 2025-03-01, 63 trading days

steps.title: The orchestrator plans the run
steps.body: It creates a run_id and resolves the ticker to a permanent entity_id, so a ticker change such as FB to META is still one company.
steps.graph: The START node writes run metadata into shared state.

steps.title: Eight agents start at once
steps.body: Each specialist gets only the data and tools for its domain. The news agent cannot run a DCF; the valuation agent cannot read headlines.
steps.graph: Send fans one node out into eight parallel branches.

steps.title: Every read goes through the as-of gate
steps.body: Every tool requires an as_of date, and the server returns only facts whose tradable_date is on or before it. For example, get_fact(ENT_000412, revenue, as_of=2025-03-01) cannot see a 10-K filed later. No agent can request the future, whatever its prompt says.
steps.graph: Tools are bound per agent. The time filter lives in the server, outside the model's control.

steps.title: The model reasons, code computes
steps.body: The fundamentals agent picks yoy_growth and the facts to feed it; Python returns 0.081. The claim it emits cites its fact_ids and filing accession numbers and must validate against a Pydantic schema.
steps.graph: Parallel branches append to claims through a reducer, so no branch overwrites another.

claims: fundamentals: FY2024 revenue +8.1% YoY, cites fact_9912 and fact_8820

steps.title: Fan-in at the evidence checker
steps.body: A separate checker confirms each cited fact exists, was tradable before as_of, recomputes the value within tolerance, and checks units and periods. It sees the claim and its sources, never the author's reasoning.
steps.graph: A join waits for every branch, or a timeout, before the checker runs.

verdicts: existence, temporal, recompute, units: pass on most claims

steps.title: One chance to fix a failed claim
steps.body: A valuation claim fails recompute. It goes back to its agent once, with the reason code. If it fails again it is dropped and logged, never quietly kept.
steps.graph: A conditional edge routes on the verdict; a revision counter in state bounds the loop to one pass.

revisions: valuation: 1 claim returned, fixed on retry

steps.title: The chief analyst decides
steps.body: It reads verified claims only, weights agents by past calibration, and states disagreements, such as expensive valuation against strong momentum, instead of voting them away.
steps.graph: A single synthesis node reads the merged, verified state.

steps.title: Calibrate, then record everything
steps.body: A calibrator fitted on past walk-forward folds adjusts the probability in code. The record stores the data snapshot, prompt version, model ID and code commit, so the run can be reproduced exactly.
steps.graph: END: the final state is written as the versioned record.

record: data snapshot, prompt v3, model ID, commit

steps.title: 63 trading days later
steps.body: When the realized outcome arrives, the harness scores the forecast with Brier score and log loss, against base-rate, calculation-only and single-agent baselines. If the agents do not beat them, that is the result reported.
steps.graph: Outside the graph: evaluation runs on stored records, never inside a live run.

score: Brier and log loss vs 3 baselines
